## Design decisions

- **`node:http`, not `fetch`** — the executed leg caught that node's undici
  unconditionally appends `Sec-Fetch-Mode`, which binding (c)'s P3/P4 gate
  refuses (`http 403`). `node:http` is the stdlib transport that can speak the
  gated wire shape (bearer + exact-Host + no Origin/`Sec-Fetch-*`), one
  `Connection: close` request per call — the same deliberately dumb transport
  as the Rust `NetClient`'s raw `TcpStream`. The binding constraint honored is
  "stdlib only, no npm dependencies"; recorded in the ADR-0050 row, not
  re-litigated.
- **Encode/decode semantics mirror `emit.rs` exactly** — absent⇒false for
  optional bools, `[]` for absent arrays, `{}` for absent maps,
  `undefined`/`None` otherwise; verified against `emit.rs:206–245` and by the
  executed leg.
- **Optional type-check leg not landed** — a meaningful `tsc --noEmit` over
  `node:http` needs `@types/node` (an npm toolchain dep beyond the ticket's
  closed posture); the executable legs carry the proof honestly.
- **Salvage** — this run resumed an interrupted worker's uncommitted drafts;
  the artifact was deleted and regenerated byte-identical before trust; the
  run ledger records the audit + the fetch defect fix.
